articles.title: Masdar Launches 35MW Battery Energy Storage System in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Masdar has commenced operations at its new 35MW battery energy storage system in Rochdale, capable of powering 35,000 homes daily and enhancing grid stability.
articles.content_html:
Masdar has officially launched its 35MW/70MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Rochdale, marking a significant step in the company's commitment to renewable energy in the UK. The facility is designed to provide enough clean power for approximately 35,000 homes each day, based on two charging and discharging cycles.

The new battery system will play a crucial role in balancing the electricity grid, responding to fluctuations in supply and demand within milliseconds. This capability is essential for maintaining grid stability, especially as the UK transitions to more renewable energy sources.

This project is the second BESS initiative by Masdar in the UK, following the successful launch of a 20MW/40MWh facility in Stockport last December. Masdar has committed to investing £1 billion in developing a 3GWh pipeline of battery storage projects across the UK, which includes additional developments in Chesterfield and Cardiff with a combined capacity of 150MW/300MWh.

Husain Al Meer, Executive Director of Global Offshore Wind & UK at Masdar, stated that the commencement of operations at the Rochdale facility is a key milestone in their investment strategy, which aims to enhance the UK's energy storage capabilities. The financing for this project was secured last month, with up to £97 million obtained from SMBC and ING.
